card.name: Linking words before co-administered drugs
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as "with", "and" or a comma right where a second drug is about to be named. Typical settings are co-administration, combination use or comparison with another therapy.

modes.label: With after co-administered or combination
modes.description: The word "with" after "co-administered" or "in combination", just before a partner drug such as methotrexate.
modes.example: KEVZARA may be used as monotherapy or in combination<< with>> methotrexate (MTX)

modes.label: Compared to those treated with
modes.description: The word "with" in comparison phrases before the comparator treatment.
modes.example: compared to those treated<< with>> TNF blockers [see Clinical Studies (

modes.label: List separators between drugs
modes.description: A comma or "and" inside a list of drug names.

card.writes: It pushes toward injection-related words, suggesting a drug name or route comes next.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label is about to name a second drug used together with or compared to the first.
